items.descriptionEn: Custom description created by the Integrated Conditioning routine importer for wger.

Sit with your feet pressed against each other, and one knee raised all the way out to the side of your body. Place your elbow on your raised knee, bend it at 90 degrees, and point your hand directly forward, holding your barbell/dumbbell. Keep your shoulder depressed and retracted, raise your hand until your forearm is vertical, as if you were about to wave at someone like a robot. Lower your hand to the original position and repeat.
items.author: Croak6728

items.descriptionEn: Deep loaded stretch for latissimus dorsi, performed after pulling movements.
Deep loaded stretch for pectorals, typically performed at end of chest work.
Deep loaded stretch for deltoids, performed after pressing movements.

Face pulls with band – standing horizontal pull. Grab the band at face height, pull elbows high and wide towards your face while squeezing shoulder blades together. Trains upper back, rear shoulders and improves posture.
items.author: 54str

items.descriptionEn: Attach a rope to a pulley station set at about chest level. Step back so you're supporting the weight with arms completely outstretched and assume a staggered (one foot forward) stance. Bend the knees slightly for a stable base. Retract the scapulae (squeeze your partner's finger with your shoulder blades) and pull the center of the rope slightly up towards the face. A good cue is to think about pulling the ends of the rope apart, not just pulling back. As you near your face, externally rotate so your knuckles are facing the ceiling. Hold for one second at the top position and slowly lower.
items.author: abeworld

items.descriptionEn: Hand Positioning: Start in a plank position with your hands directly beneath your shoulders. Spread your fingers wide apart, placing them firmly on the ground. Finger Placement: Gradually lift your palms off the ground, shifting the weight onto your fingers. Focus on distributing the load evenly across your fingertips and thumbs. Body Alignment: Maintain a straight line from head to heels to engage your core. Keep your body in a controlled and stable position throughout the exercise. Lowering Phase: Slowly bend your elbows, lowering your chest towards the ground. Ensure controlled movement, maintaining stability on your fingertips. Pushing Up: Press through your fingertips to straighten your arms, returning to the starting position. Emphasize the engagement of your fingers and thumbs throughout the push-up.
Hang for 10 seconds on a fingerboard with a 20 mm edge
items.author: marcelbader

items.descriptionEn: Fire Hydrant Circles Part of: Limber 11 Source: Joe DeFranco Prescription: 10 forward / 10 backward Type: dynamic
items.author: Pete-E automation

items.descriptionEn: Execution Start position: Elbows bent at roughly 90°, hands just outside your chest. Keep wrists straight and aligned with your forearms. Pressing phase (concentric): Push the handles forward until your arms are almost fully extended — don’t lock out. Focus on squeezing your chest at the end of the movement. Returning phase (eccentric): Slowly bring the handles back toward your chest, feeling the stretch in your pecs . Maintain tension — don’t let the weight stack touch down between reps.
items.author: daiben

items.descriptionEn: An eccentric exercise for the wrist extensors, done with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar, and widely used in rehabilitation for lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow). Hold the bar vertically in the affected hand with the wrist extended. Grasp the top of the bar with the other hand, palm facing away, and twist the top hand to wind up the bar. Bring both arms out in front of you with the bar horizontal, then slowly let the affected wrist untwist the bar over about four seconds while the other hand holds steady. Reset and repeat. The reverse version, twisting in the opposite direction for the wrist flexors, is used for medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow). Move slowly and stop if the exercise causes sharp pain rather than the expected mild discomfort.
items.author: trs1800

items.descriptionEn: Performed with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar. Rest your forearm on your thigh or a table with the palm facing down and the wrist just past the edge. Hold the bar in that hand, let the wrist drop, then extend the wrist to raise the bar, keeping the forearm still. Lower slowly, taking about three seconds. The resistance comes from twisting or bending the flexible bar, so a thicker or stiffer bar increases the load. Commonly used for wrist and forearm strengthening and for elbow tendon rehabilitation.
items.author: trs1800

items.descriptionEn: Performed with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar. Rest your forearm on your thigh or a table with the palm facing up and the wrist just past the edge. Hold the bar in that hand, let the wrist extend back, then curl the wrist up to raise the bar while the forearm stays still. Lower slowly, taking about three seconds. Works the wrist flexors, and is the companion movement to FlexBar wrist extension for balanced forearm strengthening.
items.author: trs1800

items.descriptionEn: Starting position: Sit with your arms behind you, supporting your back.Your fingers should point forward.Your knees should be bent, feet together. Steps: Raise your hips off the ground, straightening your arms. Bend your elbows, bringing your hips down. Straighten your arms, returning to the previous position. Repeat steps 2 and 3. Notes: The exercise's difficulty depends on how high you bring your hips.
items.descriptionZh: 起始姿势：坐在地上，双臂后放撑地，支撑上半身。手指要指向前方。膝盖弯曲，双脚并拢。 步骤： 抬起臀部，离开地面，伸直手臂。 弯曲肘部，臀部向下。 伸直手臂，回到之前的位置。 重复步骤2和步骤3。 注：练习难度取决于臀部撑起得有多高。

items.descriptionEn: Lie on back with heels on floor gliders or towels. Lift hips into a bridge, then slide heels toward glutes while keeping hips elevated. Slowly return to the starting position while maintaining the hip bridge.
Allowing you to safely load more weight than a regular skull crusher, lie on the floor and rest the weight on the floor in between each repetition.
items.author: Expenses7000

items.descriptionEn: -Laying on the back, lift your straightened legs from the ground at a 45 degree angle. -As your Left foot travels downward and nearly touches the floor, your Right foot should seek to reach a 90 degree angle, or as close to one as possible. -Bring your R foot down until it nearly touches the floor, and bring your L foot upwards. Maintain leg rigidity throughout the exercise. Your head should stay off the ground, supported by tightened upper abdominals. -(L up R down, L down R up, x2) ^v, v^, ^v, v^ = 1 rep -Primarily works the Rectus Abdominus, the hip flexors and the lower back. Secondarily works the Obliques. Emphasis placed on the lower quadrant of the abs.
items.author: nate303303

items.descriptionEn: cable machine, two steps forward, straight back

items.descriptionEn: Take two dumbbells and lay on a bench, make sure the feet are firmly on the ground and your back is not arched, but has good contact with the bench. The arms are stretched in front of you, about shoulder wide. Bend now the arms a bit and let them down with a half-circle movement to the side. Without changing the angle of the elbow bring them in a fluid movement back up.

items.descriptionEn: The exercise is the same as with a regular bench: Take two dumbbells and lay on a bench, make sure the feet are firmly on the ground and your back is not arched, but has good contact with the bench. The arms are stretched in front of you, about shoulder wide. Bend now the arms a bit and let them down with a half-circle movement to the side. Without changing the angle of the elbow bring them in a fluid movement back up.

items.descriptionEn: Lie face down with one leg bent out to the side and the foam roller under the inner thigh. Slowly roll back and forth over your adductors with moderate pressure.

items.descriptionEn: Slowly roll the front of your shin (tibialis anterior) over the foam roller with moderate pressure, moving back and forth.

items.descriptionEn: Sit on the foam roller and slowly roll back and forth over your glutes with moderate pressure.
items.author: Davidgj32

items.descriptionEn: Lie on your side with the foam roller under the outside of your thigh and slowly roll back and forth along the iliotibial band with moderate pressure.

items.descriptionEn: Lie face down with the foam roller under your thighs and slowly roll back and forth over your quadriceps with moderate pressure.

items.author: Anastasious

items.descriptionEn: Starting position: Stand tall with your back straight. Steps: Keeping your arms straight, bring them in front of you, move them down, behind your back, then over your head, and back to the initial position. Keep circling your arms as described in step 1.
items.descriptionZh: 起始姿势：站直 步骤： 双臂伸直，放在面前，下移，放到背后，过头，最后回到初始姿势。 如第 1 步所述，重复这套动作。

items.descriptionEn: Starting position: Sit or stand with your back straight. Steps: Place your hands on your shoulders. Repeatedly rotate both shoulder joints in a circular motion at a moderate pace.
items.descriptionZh: 起始姿势：坐位或站位，背部挺直。 步骤： 将双手放在肩膀上。 以适中的速度不断绕转两侧肩关节。

items.descriptionEn: Starting position: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing forward, facing a wall or bench for support if needed. Bend your knees into a squat position. Place your hands on the ground in front of you, shoulder-width apart, with your fingers spread wide. Make sure your elbows are under your shoulders and your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels. Upward phase: Push with your feet and hands to lift your body off the ground. Straighten your legs and arms, keeping your body aligned. Engage your core and glutes to maintain the position. If needed, rest your knees on the wall or bench for assistance.
items.author: clafal

items.descriptionEn: Get on your hands and knees. Widen your knees outwards, and drop to your elbows. Without moving your elbows or knees, start to rock forwards and backwards, trying to get your bum closer to your feet.
